summary: Iteration 7 tested the 15 new paid templates. Backend: the new test_iteration7_paid_templates.py passes 43/43, and the full regression suite passes 123/123 when run serially (-n 0). Verified: GET /api/products returns 20 products; all 15 new products have the correct INR price (none at 0), category and file_name; all 15 detail endpoints work; each new product has a storage_path in Mongo. For each of the 15 I created a checkout, set the order to paid in Mongo, and downloaded the file: PDFs come back as application/pdf starting with %PDF, and the 7 bundles come back as application/zip containing a valid .pdf and a valid .xlsx. Unpaid and pending_review orders still get 404 on download. EARLY20 on freelancer-finance gives 399, GPay submit goes to pending_review, free checkout still works, and all admin endpoints return 401/403 without auth. Frontend (1920 and 390): 20 cards, prices shown in ₹, every category filter shows the expected count (Finance 3, Business 4, Home 2, Career 1, Wellbeing 1, Financial tracker 1, Budgeting 1, Planning 3), searching 'tracker' returns 5 products, no broken images, no horizontal overflow, no console errors. The 7 requested products show the correct price in quick view and on the product page, the workbook preview opens, and checkout auto-applies EARLY20 with the struck-through price and a 'Continue to GPay' button. One job-search checkout went through to the /pay page (₹159, GPay number shown); no payment was submitted. Main finding: the downloadable files are mostly generic and identical across products (details below).

minor.issue: The new limit of 3 free claims per email per hour is easy to get around by changing the email address, and it is not limited by IP. It also broke 3 earlier regression tests that reused one fixed email; I fixed the tests.

ui_bugs.issue: The data-testid is built from the raw category name, so it can contain spaces ('category-financial tracker', 'category-free templates'). Use a slug instead (replace spaces with '-').

issues: There are now 12 pills plus the search box in one row. 'Financial tracker' and 'Free templates' wrap onto two lines, and the row looks cramped. Consider white-space:nowrap with horizontal scroll, or merging categories (Finance, Financial tracker and Budgeting overlap heavily).
The pills scroll horizontally and 'Planning' is cut off with no scroll hint, so 8 of the 12 categories are hidden off screen.

Products are sorted by created_at descending, so the original bestsellers (Weekly Reset, Quiet Brand Kit) and the free templates are now at the very bottom, below 15 new items. Consider a curated order or sort field.

The preview is the same generic placeholder for every product ('A gentler way to plan' / 'A prompt to begin'). It does not show the real pages of, for example, the Money Map or Freelancer Finance product.
Content Batch Planner uses the same Unsplash photo as Slow Content Calendar (photo-1499750310107).

product_content_issues: HIGH (customer trust): the paid deliverables are templated and almost identical. All 7 finance PDFs (Money Map, Monthly Budget, Debt Payoff, Savings Goals, Subscription Audit, Income & Invoice, Freelancer Finance) have the same 3 inner pages: a Date/Description/Category/In/Out/Balance table, a 'Money with intention' prompt page and a weekly check-in. Debt Payoff has no debt list or snowball/avalanche page, Savings Goals has no goal milestones, and Subscription Audit has no subscription list.

HIGH: Client Onboarding, Project Scope, Meeting Notes, Meal & Grocery, Home Reset and Self-Care all have the same 2 generic prompt pages ('What is true right now', 'The kind boundary', 'Today/This week/Later'). Only the description line differs. The Meal & Grocery Planner has no meal grid or grocery list, and the Self-Care Habit Tracker has no habit grid. Confirmed by rendering the pages.

HIGH: all 7 XLSX files are the same sheet (Date/Description/Category/Planned/Actual/Notes, 20 rows, 2 SUM formulas). Job Search Tracker and Content Batch Planner get ₹ Planned/Actual columns, which do not fit those products. The Income & Invoice tracker has no invoice number, due date or status. Freelancer Finance (₹499, Premium) has no tax or irregular-income logic.
The descriptions promise specific features (sinking funds, payoff strategy, taxes, interview notes) that the files do not contain. make_paid_templates.py needs per-product page and sheet definitions.
action_items: Rewrite make_paid_templates.py so each product gets content that matches its description: debt list and payoff strategy, savings milestones, subscription audit table, invoice log with number/due date/status, freelancer tax set-aside, meal grid plus grocery list, habit grid, job application pipeline, content batch calendar, meeting decisions/owners, project scope deliverables. Give the XLSX product-specific columns. Then regenerate the files and re-upload them. upload_seed_files skips products that already have a storage_path, so clear the storage_path first or add a version check.
Make the workbook preview product-specific, or at least use each product's real page titles
Improve the filter row: nowrap pills, fewer or merged categories, a scroll hint on mobile
Consider a curated product sort so the bestsellers and free items are not buried
Use slugs for the category-pill data-testid
Give Content Batch Planner its own image
critical_code_review_comments: upload_seed_files() never re-uploads a file once storage_path exists, so regenerated seed assets will not reach storage on deploy. Add a file hash or version to the product doc.
seed() uses $setOnInsert, so later changes to SEED names, prices or descriptions are never applied to existing DB rows. That is fine for owner edits, but there is no migration path.
Carried over: is_admin() fails open when CLERK_SECRET_KEY == ''.
App.js is a 34KB minified-style single file with 37 very long lines, which is hard to maintain or review. Split it into components.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Run the full suite with: export REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=$(grep REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL /app/frontend/.env | cut -d= -f2); pytest tests/ -n 0. Earlier test files read the env var at import time. test_iteration7 marks orders paid directly via pymongo (loads backend/.env through dotenv without printing it). Quick-view button testid is quick-view-{id}; the modal is quick-view-modal with a quick-view-close button. Free checkout is limited to 3 per email per hour, so use unique emails. Retest the regenerated template contents once main agent rewrites make_paid_templates.py.
